title: Rabbi Zinon the Chazzan
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman relates that in Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot, chapter 4, end of halakhah 1, and Taanit, chapter 4, end of halakhah 1, when they removed Rabban Gamliel from his patriarchate and told Rabbi Chutzpit the meturgeman, “Dismiss the people,” they told Rabbi Zinon the chazzan, “Speak.” In his account, Zinon began and said, “Upon whom has your wickedness not passed continually?” Hyman infers that he was the attendant of the congregation in the Sanhedrin of Yavneh.

notes.text: Hyman’s inference about the person is retained as his inference. The named witness’s collective speakers and the notice’s Zinon framing are not silently equated.

The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 4:1 has the assembled people speak the verse after Zinon begins. Hyman’s compressed account puts the words after “he began and said”; the translation preserves his account without equating its speaker framing with the consulted witness.
